title: SYSK Selects: How Narco States Work
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the December 2009 episode "How Narco States Work." Josh and Chuck define a narco state as a region or country where the government is directly involved in or turns a blind eye to drug trafficking. They discuss how the drug trade and corruption take hold (eroded social contract, assassinations of officials, bribery, compromised intelligence services, poverty, unstable post-civil-war regions, and abundant guns), the economics of cocaine and heroin markups, and examples including Afghanistan's poppy trade, Guatemala, Colombia and FARC, Cold War proxy wars, Manuel Noriega in Panama, the School of the Americas, Zambia, Senegal, and Guinea-Bissau. The episode closes with a listener email about British DNA database practices for crime victims.

segments.title: Opening banter and Selects introduction
segments.summary: Chuck introduces the Selects rerun of the December 2009 episode. Josh and Chuck banter about Mexico border towns and loosely define a narco state as a place where the government allows or participates in drug trafficking, noting that they are usually regions rather than whole countries, with Afghanistan and Guinea-Bissau cited as examples.

segments.title: Drug flows and the global drug market
segments.summary: The hosts explain that drugs entering the US usually come through Mexico and Central America after the Caribbean route was shut down in the 1990s. They note Americans' cocaine consumption and Europe's heroin addiction, compare street prices of a kilo of cocaine in the US and Moscow, and cite an estimated global drug trade of about $300 billion a year.

segments.title: Social contract and how states become narco states
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck discuss Hobbes's social contract and the state's monopoly on violence. They describe how a state can lose control through assassinations of officials by cartels, bribery of politicians, compromised intelligence services, and collapsed infrastructure after civil wars, with poor countries flooded with guns and former soldiers being especially vulnerable.
topics: FARC attack on Colombian justice building

segments.title: Afghanistan poppy production and government involvement
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Afghanistan's dependence on heroin for much of its GDP, President Hamid Karzai's reported reluctance to allow aerial spraying of poppy fields, US commanders' frustrations with the DEA, and record poppy harvests. They contrast this with Colombia, where aerial eradication of coca was used with a friendlier president.

segments.title: Guatemala, Central America, and Cold War roots
segments.summary: The hosts describe a Guatemalan federal judge accused of accepting bribes to dismiss a drug case, legislation blocking extradition, and a reported five-to-one ratio of illegal guns to legitimate ones in Central America. They trace the region's instability to Cold War proxy wars between the US and USSR, with FARC's reputation for brutality and US-backed paramilitary and dictatorship groups.

segments.title: US involvement, Noriega, School of the Americas, and Africa
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the Reagan-era war on drugs alongside US support for anti-communist groups tied to cocaine, Manuel Noriega's CIA ties and 1989 removal from Panama, and the School of the Americas training of figures later tied to cartels. They then turn to Africa, where Zambia's marijuana trade and Senegal's rising heroin and cocaine trade were early examples, and a 2008 Telegraph report put a bribe at the airport at nine thousand dollars per kilo.

segments.title: Guinea-Bissau as a narco state
segments.summary: The hosts describe Guinea-Bissau as the one functioning narco state, with about $150 million of cocaine passing through each month, roughly half the national GDP. They recount how fishermen found packages of cocaine in 2005, used it as fertilizer, and were then paid by a South American man, and describe a 2006 incident in which soldiers took seized cocaine and two Colombian suspects from police, and the military's later killing of the president.

segments.title: Wrap-up and promo
segments.summary: The hosts wrap up the narco states topic and point listeners to the HowStuffWorks article on narco states.
